'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Terrorism in Indonesia]]
**[[Jakarta School bombing]]
***Ninety-six people are injured, some critically, in a bombing at a mosque inside a school in [[Jakarta]], [[Indonesia]]. A 17-year-old male is identified as the perpetrator and later recovered at a hospital, [[right-wing terrorism]] is suspected. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/explosion-school-complex-indonesias-jakarta-local-media-reports-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clykgdg3l42o (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Serbia]]'s [[National Assembly (Serbia)|parliament]] passes a [[Law of Serbia|law]] to expedite construction of [[Trump Tower Belgrade]] on the former [[Yugoslavia|Yugoslav]] [[General Staff Building, Belgrade|defence ministry site]] in [[Savski Venac]], [[Belgrade]], despite protests from opponents who want the [[NATO bombing of Yugoslavia|damaged buildings]] preserved. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/serbian-parliament-supports-kushners-project-despite-opposition-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Pacific typhoon season]]
**The death toll from [[Typhoon Kalmaegi]]'s impact on the [[Philippines]] rises to at least 188, with at least 135 others missing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c70jnx9e414o (BBC News)]
**Typhoon Kalmaegi makes [[landfall]] in [[Central Vietnam|central]] [[Vietnam]], killing at least five people in [[Daklak province|Daklak]] and [[Gia Lai province|Gia Lai]] and leaving three others missing in [[Quảng Ngãi province|Quảng Ngãi]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/typhoon-kalmaegi-kills-5-people-vietnam-philippines-prepares-127285098 (AP via ABC News)]
*[[2025 Rio Bonito do Iguaçu tornado]]
**A [[tornado]], rated F3 on the [[Fujita scale]], strikes [[Rio Bonito do Iguaçu]], [[Brazil]], killing at least six people and injuring 432 others. [https://oglobo.globo.com/brasil/noticia/2025/11/07/tornado-arrasa-cidade-no-interior-no-parana-prefeito-relata-tres-mortes.ghtml (''O Globo'')] [https://www.parana.pr.gov.br/aen/Noticia/Municipio-de-Rio-Bonito-do-Iguacu-foi-atingido-por-um-tornado-confirma-Simepar (Paraná)]
*Five people are killed and two others are injured when a [[Kamov Ka-226]] passenger helicopter crashes in [[Achi-Su]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]]. [https://aviation-safety.net/wikibase/561628 (ASN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2020–2025 H5N1 outbreak]]
**[[2025 Canadian ostrich culling controversy]]
***[[Canada]]'s [[Canadian Food Inspection Agency|food inspection agency]] confirms that a [[marksman]] has [[Culling|culled]] all 300–330 [[ostrich]]es at a farm in [[Edgewood, British Columbia|Edgewood]], [[British Columbia]], under a [[Avian influenza|bird flu]] containment order, following a [[Supreme Court of Canada|Supreme Court]] decision allowing the cull to proceed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4gzl9d759po (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda relations]]
**[[2025 Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda peace agreement]]
***The [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] and [[Rwanda]] state that they have agreed on a Regional Economic Integration Framework in [[Washington, D.C.]], [[United States]], to expand economic cooperation and subject to conditions including the withdrawal of [[Rwandan Defence Force|Rwandan forces]] from eastern Congo and operations against the [[Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-rwanda-initial-economic-framework-washington-part-peace-process-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Australia–Nauru relations]], [[Nauru Regional Processing Centre]]
**[[Australia]] begins to deport hundreds of non-citizens to [[Nauru]], as part of a bilateral agreement between both countries, in which Australia will pay Nauru [[Australian dollar|A$]]2.5 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]1.6 billion) over 30 years in exchange for Nauru issuing [[Visa policy of Nauru|visas]] to these individuals deported from Australia. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/578139/australia-begins-deporting-non-citizens-to-nauru-under-multimillion-dollar-resettlement-plan (RNZ)]
*[[China–Japan relations]], [[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]]
**[[Japan]] reports that [[Economy of Japan|seafood exports]] to [[China]] have resumed for the first time since China imposed a ban in August 2023 over [[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|treated wastewater releases]] from the [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant]]. However, China maintains restrictions on products from [[Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima]] and surrounding [[Prefectures of Japan|prefectures]]. [https://apnews.com/article/japan-china-seafood-export-fukushima-nuclear-9acffde0a742704428864490a1433317 (AP)]
*[[Hungary–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] grants [[Hungary]] a one-year exemption from [[Embargo of Russian oil during the Russo-Ukrainian war|sanctions]] on [[Russia]]n [[Petroleum industry in Russia|oil and gas]], with Hungary agreeing to purchase [[Petroleum in the United States|U.S. liquefied natural gas]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-meet-hungarys-orban-discuss-russian-oil-economic-cooperation-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Indonesia–United Kingdom relations]], [[Capital punishment in Indonesia]]
**[[Indonesia]] repatriates [[British people|British]] nationals [[Lindsay Sandiford]], sentenced to death for [[Drug trafficking in Indonesia|smuggling]] [[cocaine]] into [[Bali]] in 2013, and Shahab Shahabadi, who was serving a [[Life imprisonment|life sentence]] for drug offences, following a bilateral agreement on humanitarian grounds. Both are transferred to the [[United Kingdom]] to serve the remainder of their sentences under [[Law of the United Kingdom|UK law]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/british-woman-death-row-leaves-indonesia-after-repatriation-deal-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russia–European Union relations]], [[Government and intergovernmental reactions to the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**The [[European Union]] ends the issuance of multiple-entry [[Visa policy of the Schengen Area|Schengen visa]]s to [[Russian citizenship law|Russian citizens]], citing security concerns linked to the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]], alleged sabotage, and visa misuse, while allowing exceptions for [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|dissidents]], journalists, [[Human rights in Russia|human rights]] defenders, and close family members of [[European Union citizenship|EU citizens]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-schengen-visas-russia-multiple-entry-dc830d5f208539d91a5e18948280a5a9 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Tanzanian election protests]]
**Prosecutors in [[Tanzania]] charge 98 people with [[treason]] over their alleged participation in violent protests against the [[2025 Tanzanian general election|re-election]] of [[President of Tanzania|President]] [[Samia Suluhu Hassan]] last week. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tanzania-charges-98-people-with-treason-over-election-protests-filings-show-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Poland]]'s [[Sejm]] removes former [[Ministry of Justice (Poland)|justice minister]] [[Zbigniew Ziobro]]'s [[Parliamentary immunity|immunity]], clearing the way for prosecutors to charge him with 26 offences, including [[abuse of power]] and [[Corruption in Poland|misuse of public funds]] from the [[Ministry of Funds and Regional Policy|Justice Fund]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/polish-parliament-strips-former-justice-minister-immunity-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Law enforcement in Spain|Police]] in [[Spain]] arrest 13 alleged members of the [[Venezuela]]n gang [[Tren de Aragua]] in a coordinated operation in five cities. [https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-drugs-gang-trafficking-spain-b1ee090d631c551fc4fbbfa12eaa7924 (AP)]
